key_insight: Incorporating mask-based priors into denoising diffusion models guides sequence generation to better satisfy structural constraints, improving accuracy and controllability in inverse protein folding (this item is an author correction clarifying the original result).
problem_solved: Designing amino-acid sequences that reliably fold to a target 3D structure is ambiguous and hard to control; the paper addresses how to condition generative models so designs respect partial or full structural constraints and yield higher-quality, designable proteins.
method: Mask-prior-guided denoising diffusion: inject structure-derived mask information as a conditioning prior into the forward/backward diffusion process so the model focuses sampling on compatible residues.
Structure-conditioned learning: train the diffusion model on protein sequence–structure pairs with objectives that reinforce masked-region fidelity and overall sequence plausibility.
Flexible inference: support partial masks (user-specified constraints) and produce diverse high-confidence sequence candidates that better recover target folds.
impact: Provides a practical, controllable generative approach for structure-conditioned protein design, improving success rates for inverse folding tasks and enabling ML practitioners to incorporate explicit constraints into diffusion-based sequence generation.
visual_elements: Schematic of diffusion pipeline showing mask prior injected into the denoising steps (before vs after comparison).
Side-by-side protein ribbon visualization: target structure with masked regions and resulting designed sequence mapped onto the structure.
Bar chart comparing folding/recovery metrics (e.g., fold accuracy, sequence validity, diversity) between baseline diffusion and mask-prior-guided method.
Flowchart of usage: input structure + mask → conditioned sampling → candidate sequences → structure prediction/validation.
paper_title: Author Correction: Mask-prior-guided denoising diffusion improves inverse protein folding
paper_authors: Peizhen Bai, Filip Miljković, Xianyuan Liu, Leonardo De Maria, Rebecca Croasdale-Wood
